source.notes: Paper prints: Series SQRP1, 'SET~1' (text layer; stored as SET-1), Q.P. Code 56/1/1, 23 printed pages (24 PDF pages incl. a trailing blank), 33 questions, Maximum Marks 70, Time allowed 3 hours. Session is not printed on the paper. Each page carries bilingual Hindi+English content followed by a pure-English repeat page; question/page numbers reference the pure-English page. Section A (1-16) is MCQ/Assertion-Reason (1 mark); Section B (17-21) very short answer (2 marks); Section C (22-28) short answer (3 marks); Section D (29-30) case-based with internal choice in one sub-part each (4 marks); Section E (31-33) long answer/numerical, each with a full internal-choice alternative (5 marks). Many multi-part questions print a stray digit (e.g. '3  1') after the marks value in the source PDF; this was treated as an unexplained footnote/layout artifact, not an additional mark, and the printed section-level mark was used. The official marking scheme is heavy with hand-drawn structures, reaction schemes and multi-line calculations that render as images and are not present in its text layer (flagged per question); where nothing at all was recoverable, officialAnswer is omitted and the gap is noted in extractionIssues.

questions.text:
What type of deviation from Raoult’s law is shown by a mixture of phenol and aniline ? Give reason.
What will happen to the boiling point of the solution on mixing phenol and aniline ?

officialAnswer.text:
Negative deviation.
Solute-solvent interactions are stronger than solute-solute and solvent-solvent interactions. / The intermolecular hydrogen bonding between the phenolic proton and the lone pair on the nitrogen atom of aniline is stronger than the respective intermolecular hydrogen bonding between similar molecules.
Boiling point of the solution increases.

questions.text: Why are haloarenes less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction ? Give two reasons.

officialAnswer.text:
Because of:
(i) C–X acquires partial double bond character due to resonance
(ii) sp2 hybridisation of the C of C–X makes it more electronegative and holds the electron pair tightly
(iii) repulsion between the nucleophile and the electron-rich arene ring
(iv) instability of the phenyl cation
(Any two)

questions.text:
Differentiate between the following :
(i) Peptide linkage and Glycosidic linkage
(ii) Essential amino acids and Non-essential amino acids

officialAnswer.text:
(i) It is an amide linkage formed between two amino acids through –CONH– / an amide linkage formed between –COOH and –NH2 groups, whereas in glycosidic linkage two or more monosaccharides are joined together by an oxygen atom.
(ii) Those which cannot be synthesised in the body and must be obtained through diet are known as essential amino acids. The amino acids which can be synthesised in the body are known as non-essential amino acids.

questions.text:
Following reaction takes place in one step :
2A + B → 2C
How will the rate of above reaction change if the volume of the reaction vessel is decreased to one third of its original volume ? Will there be any change in the order of reaction with the reduced volume ?
extractionIssues: Reaction arrow reconstructed (printed as a dash in the text layer)
Official-answer equals signs and exponents lost in extraction; rebuilt from spacing/context (rate law k[A]²[B]); check against the marking scheme PDF

officialAnswer.text:
Rate = k[A]²[B]. If the volume is decreased to 1/3rd of the original, concentration increases 3 times.
Rate′ = k[3A]²[3B] = 27 k[A]²[B]
Hence rate will be increased by 27 times.
Order remains same.

questions.text:
The reaction of amines with mineral acids to form ammonium salts shows that these are basic in nature. Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia whereas aromatic amines are weaker bases than ammonia. Aliphatic and aromatic primary and secondary amines react with acid chlorides, anhydrides and esters by nucleophilic substitution reaction. The main problem encountered during electrophilic substitution reactions of aromatic amines is that of their high reactivity. Substitution tends to occur at ortho-and para-positions. Hinsberg reagent is used for the identification and distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Aryldiazonium salts, usually obtained from arylamines, undergo replacement of the diazonium group with a variety of nucleophiles to provide advantageous methods for producing aryl halides, cyanides, phenols and arenes.
Answer the following questions :
(a) (i) Why CH3 – NH2 is a stronger base than (CH3)3N in aqueous solution ?
(ii) Write structural formulae of the compound A and B :
CH3CONH2 –(NaOBr / Base)→ A –(C6H5COCl)→ B
(b) A compound ‘X’ with molecular formula C3H9N reacts with Hinsberg reagent to give a product insoluble in alkali. Identify ‘X’.
OR
(b) How can you convert aniline to benzonitrile ?
(c) Why is –NH2 group of aniline acetylated before carrying out nitration ?
extractionIssues: Subscripts flattened: CH3–NH2, (CH3)3N, C3H9N, CH3CONH2, C6H5COCl, C6H5
Sub-part marks shown in brackets ('2 1', '1') were printed in the margin; total of 4(2+1+1) taken from the section header

officialAnswer.text:
(a) (i) Due to combined effect of the inductive effect, solvation effect and steric hinderance of the alkyl group.
(ii) A = CH3NH2, B = CH3NHCOC6H5
(b) CH3CH2NHCH3 / N-Methylethanamine
OR
(b) [conversion of aniline to benzonitrile – reaction scheme is an image in the marking scheme, not extracted]
(c) The nitration reaction can be controlled and the p-nitro derivative can be obtained as the major product / To prevent the formation of anilinium ion which is meta directing.

questions.text:
The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometry of coordination compounds. The Crystal Field Theory (CFT) of coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by the ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields.
Answer the following questions :
(a) In octahedral crystal field, energies of which d-orbitals will be raised when ligands approach the central metal atom/ion ? Give reason in support of your answer.
(b) Using crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration of central metal atom/ion of the following :
(i) [CoF6]3–
(ii) [Co(NH3)6]3+ [At. No. : Co = 27]
(c) [NiCl4]2– is paramagnetic while [Ni(CO)4] is diamagnetic though both are tetrahedral. Why ? [Atomic No. : Ni = 28]
OR
(c) Write hybridization and magnetic behaviour of the complex [Fe(CN)6]3–. [Atomic No. : Fe = 26]
extractionIssues: Subscripts/superscripts flattened: [CoF6]3–, [Co(NH3)6]3+, [NiCl4]2–, [Ni(CO)4], [Fe(CN)6]3–

officialAnswer.text:
(a) dx²–y² and dz² orbitals. In octahedral crystal field, ligands approach the metal atom/ion along the axis, due to which dx²–y² and dz² orbitals experience more repulsion (their energies are raised).
(b) (i) [CoF6]3–: Co3+ = 3d6
(ii) [Co(NH3)6]3+: Co3+ = 3d6
(c) In [NiCl4]2–, Cl– is a weak field ligand and does not pair up the unpaired electrons in the 3d-orbital, hence paramagnetic. In [Ni(CO)4], CO being a strong field ligand pairs up the unpaired electrons, hence diamagnetic.
OR
(c) Hybridisation – d2sp3. Magnetic behaviour: Paramagnetic.

questions.text:
(i) From the given data of E° values, answer the following questions :
E°(M2+/M) (V) – Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu : –1.18, –0.91, –1.18, –0.44, –0.28, –0.25, +0.34
(I) Why does E°(M2+/M) show irregular trend in the above values ?
(II) Why is E°(Cu2+/Cu) value exceptionally positive ?
(III) Why is E°(Mn2+/Mn) value highly negative ?
(ii) Write the ionic equations for the oxidising action of potassium permanganate for its reaction with I– in both acidic and alkaline solutions.
extractionIssues: The E°(M2+/M) data table lists 6 element labels (Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu) but 7 numeric values in the extracted text layer; the alignment between elements and values is uncertain – see PDF page 21

(i) (I) Due to the irregular variation of ionisation enthalpies (ΔiH1+ΔiH2) and sublimation enthalpies.
(II) Due to low ΔhydH° and high ΔaH° of Cu.
(III) Because Mn2+ is highly stable due to half-filled 3d5 configuration.
